extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities (chemical manufacturers, importers, distributors, and employers), OSHA compliance officers, State Plan agencies, small business stakeholders, OMB reviewers, and rulemaking commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and supporting analyses for OSHA's final Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200), including economic/regulatory analyses, Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) information collection review, federalism/state-plan considerations, environmental/tribal reviews, and the Summary & Explanation of regulatory text changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and estimate of number of small entities (RFA requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of and an estimate of the number of small entities to which the rule will apply or an explanation of why no such estimate is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA provides tables (e.g., Table VI-2 and Table VI-3) estimating affected establishments and firms (e.g., 114,585 establishments within 106,017 private firms; 84,754 very small establishments within 83,952 firms). Include industry breakdown in the Final Economic Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of projected reporting, recordkeeping, and compliance requirements (PRA/RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the projected reporting, recordkeeping and other compliance requirements of the rule, including an estimate of the classes of small entities which will be subject to the requirements and the type of professional skills necessary for preparation of the report or record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble should describe the substantive revisions (e.g., updated hazard classification criteria, label requirements, SDS content, definitions), identify affected NAICS industries, and quantify unit burdens and required professional skills. Examples provided: SDS reclassification burdens (Health & Safety Specialist, $61.18/hr) — medium establishments: 1.5 hrs/SDS; small: 2.1 hrs/SDS; appendix language revisions: medium 0.5 hrs/SDS, small 0.7 hrs/SDS; management familiarization: medium directly affected 4.0 hrs/establishment, medium indirectly 1.0 hr, small directly 1.0 hr, small indirectly 0.25 hr; training costs per firm: 2.5 hrs Health & Safety Specialist ($61.18/hr), 0.2 hrs Logistics Personnel ($60.37/hr), 0.2 hrs Production Worker ($31.09/hr). Also quantify cost savings (e.g., $0.058 per label for very small containers) and avoided percentage losses (0.009%–0.025%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to have a written hazard communication program (substantive regulatory requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: All affected establishments must have a written hazard communication program explaining how the establishment meets the criteria of the standard with respect to labeling, SDSs, and worker information and training as discussed under paragraph (e) of the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program must describe how the employer complies with labeling, SDS, and training requirements; discussed in preamble and subject to compliance deadlines in paragraph (j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical manufacturer/importer obligation to classify chemicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical manufacturers and importers must evaluate chemicals produced in their workplaces or imported by them to classify the chemicals in accordance with the standard, determining hazard classes and, where appropriate, the category of each class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers are not required to classify chemicals if they rely on the manufacturer's or importer's classification to satisfy the requirement. Preamble explains scope and who bears classification responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steps to minimize significant economic impact on small entities (RFA/alternatives analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the steps the agency has taken to minimize the significant economic impact on small entities consistent with the stated objectives of the applicable statutes, including a statement of the factual, policy, and legal reasons for selecting the alternative adopted and why other significant alternatives were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA describes chosen implementation schedule to reduce small-entity impacts; provides factual, policy, and legal reasons for chosen alternatives and rejection of others. Example: implementation timeline balances worker safety and small business economic interests and is supported by the economic analysis and public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation schedule and compliance deadlines (minimization tool)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific compliance dates and implementation schedule intended to minimize impacts on small employers and balance safety and economic concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule compliance deadlines: chemical manufacturers/importers/distributors and employers evaluating substances — compliance with modified provisions no later than 18 months after effective date (paragraph (j)(2)(i)); for mixtures 36 months after effective date (paragraph (j)(3)(i)). Employers must update alternative workplace labeling, hazard communication programs, and provide additional employee training for newly identified hazards no later than 24 months after effective date for substances and 42 months for mixtures (paragraphs (j)(2)(ii) and (j)(3)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — OMB approval & display of control number
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, a Federal agency cannot conduct or sponsor a collection of information unless OMB approves it and the agency displays a currently valid OMB control number. No employer shall be subject to penalty for failing to comply with a collection if the collection does not display a valid OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA updated the existing paperwork package under OMB Control Number 1218-0072, prepared and submitted an ICR concurrent with the final rule, and will publish OMB review results separately. OMB issued a Notice of Action that prior clearance terms remain in effect pending final review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of comments on information collection requirements (PRA public-comment criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: When soliciting public comments under the PRA, the agency should ask whether collections are necessary, the accuracy of burden estimates, the quality/utility/clarity of information to be collected, and ways to minimize compliance burden (including automation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA solicited these comments in the NPRM and considered responses in preparing the revised ICR. Example commenters and summaries are noted in the preamble. Agencies should summarize comments and changes for OMB as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific ICR revisions to regulatory text (paragraph-level changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final ICR and regulatory text revisions modify specific paragraphs to clarify collection requirements and add/adjust label and SDS provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA identified specific modifications: (1) clarify paragraph (d)(1) hazards required to be classified; (2) add language to (f)(1) re: hazards under (d)(1)(ii) not required on shipped container labels; (3) revise (f)(5) to add two provisions related to bulk shipments; (4) revise (f)(11) to add flexibility for updating labels for products released for shipment; (5) add (f)(12) for limited labeling for small containers; (6) clarify (g)(2); and (7) add language in (i) for claiming concentrations/concentration ranges as trade secrets on SDSs. See Table VII.1 in preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICR burden estimates and summary statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide summary information about the Information Collection Request: control number, affected public, number of respondents, frequency, number of responses, average time per response, total annual burden hours and estimated annual total cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA lists: OMB Control Number 1218-0072; Affected Public: Business or other for-profit; Number of Respondents: 5,580,906; Number of Responses: 98,762,005; Estimated Annual Total Burden Hours: 7,206,569; Estimated Annual Total Cost (O&M): $69,207,596. 'Average time per response' and 'Frequency of responses' vary by reporting requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism review requirements (E.O. 13132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must, to the extent possible, refrain from limiting State policy options, consult with States before taking actions that would restrict State policy options, and limit preemption of State law to the minimum necessary to achieve statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preemption is allowed only as provided by Congress or where State law conflicts with Federal law. State Plan standards must be at least as effective as the Federal standard; where applicable to interstate commerce, State requirements must be required by compelling local conditions and not unduly burden interstate commerce. OSHA reaffirmed prior finding that promulgation complies with E.O. 13132.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Plan amendment/adoption requirement and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: When Federal OSHA issues a new or more stringent standard, OSHA-approved State Plans must either amend their standards to reflect the new federal standard or demonstrate why such action is unnecessary within a specified timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Plans must adopt the Federal standard or complete their own standard within six months of promulgation. OSHA lists the States and territories with approved State Plans and those with plans covering state/local government employees only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the final rule imposes an unfunded Federal intergovernmental or private-sector mandate with expenditures exceeding the statutory threshold (currently $100 million) and certify appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA reviewed the rule under UMRA and concluded it would not impose a Federal mandate on the private sector in excess of $100 million in any one year, and therefore certified non-applicability for UMRA-triggering thresholds. Also determine whether tribal governments would be required to expend $100M or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's health/safety evaluation (E.O. 13045)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'covered regulatory actions', evaluate environmental health or safety effects that may disproportionately affect children and explain why the planned regulation is preferable to other effective and reasonably feasible alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule is 'covered' if it is economically significant under E.O. 12866 and concerns risks that may disproportionately affect children (e.g., exposure pathways). OSHA determined this final rule is not significant under E.O. 12866 and does not present a disproportionate risk to children.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA environmental impacts assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the final rule under NEPA, CEQ regulations, and agency NEPA procedures to determine if the rule will have impacts on air, water, soil, plant or animal life, land use, or other environmental aspects and whether a significant environmental impact exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA's preliminary determination in the NPRM was no impact on environmental media or species; no commenters challenged this; final determination: regulatory changes will have no significant environmental impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and coordination with Indian Tribal Governments (E.O. 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the rule has tribal implications (direct effects on tribes, relationships with the Federal government, or distribution of power/responsibility) and consult as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA reviewed the rule under E.O. 13175 and determined it does not have tribal implications as defined by the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of GHS revision and alignment with international partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for deciding which GHS revision to align with (e.g., Rev. 7 vs Rev. 8): alignment with trading partners, improvements to hazard communication, timeliness, and worker protection considerations, while considering stakeholder input about harmonization risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA explained reasons for aligning largely with Rev. 7 (alignment with Canada, EU, Australia, New Zealand) while selectively adopting some Rev. 8 provisions that improve worker safety and clarity. The preamble discusses commenter support and opposition, concerns about selective adoption causing misalignment, and OSHA's balancing of harmonization vs. worker protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding reclassification requirement when consensus standards updated (incorporation by reference guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When updating incorporated consensus standards by reference, OSHA does not intend to require chemicals already classified using an earlier version of a consensus standard to be reclassified; retain earlier versions where relevant to avoid implying retesting is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA considered but declined to include a DATES provision exempting chemicals classified before the effective date from reclassification; instead, OSHA retained references to older versions where relevant and clarified this in Appendix B discussion. For transport tests, either Rev. 4 or Rev. 6 may be acceptable where noted; specific citations updated where new material exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Update incorporation-by-reference section (29 CFR 1910.6) to include up-to-date national and international consensus standards as proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA finalizes proposed references with limited exceptions (e.g., corrected citation spotted by DOD). OSHA will consider broader bulk updates to consensus standard references in future rulemakings per industry comment (ASTM suggestion).
